about: Measured values of a preprint (not peer reviewed), in the format of thermoml_<id>.json. DL-methyl lactate, mass fraction purity 0.98424 (GC, supplier's certificate; Macklin). Critical temperature and pressure by the pulse-heating method (the compound decomposes near its critical point; the apparent values were extrapolated to zero heating time and corrected, section 2.2), expanded uncertainties 1.5 % (Tc) and 4.5 % (pc) at 95 % confidence; the authors' acentric factor, from their Tc, pc and a vapour-pressure equation, is 0.435 (Table 4), for comparison only. Heat capacity: DSC, three-step method, corrected from the two-phase to the isobaric heat capacity; U_r = 3 % (95 %). The values here are the authors' Eq. (24) with their Table 5 constants, at 298.15 K and every 10 K within its range (298.1-417.1 K); the raw points are in a supplementary table that is not in the preprint file; Eq. (24) gives 229.81 J/(mol K) at 298.15 K, as Table 6 prints. Thermal conductivity: computed by the authors from their measured thermal diffusivity (laser flash, U_r = 5 %), their heat capacity and the densities of Lomba et al.; U_r = 8.5 % (95 %); here from their Eq. (27), lambda = d0 - d1 T, over 303-373 K. The normal boiling temperature in Table 3 is quoted from earlier articles (Lecat, 417.0 K), not measured here.

source.citation: N.S. Bogatishcheva, A.P. Popov, M.Z. Faizullin, I.S. Romanov, S.V. Portnova, E.D. Nikitin, Experimental critical pressures, temperatures, thermal diffusivities, and heat capacities of methyl, ethyl, propyl, butyl, and pentyl lactates, SSRN preprint (2026), not peer reviewed
